title: Board of Peace's Mladenov Warns Gaza Ceasefire 'Threatens a Collapse' in Al Jazeera Interview
detail: August 28, 2026 — Two days after telling the UN Security Council a collapse would be an irreversible 'point of no return,' Board of Peace High Representative Nikolay Mladenov gave a Friday interview to Al Jazeera reiterating that the failure of both Israel and Hamas to adhere to the peace roadmap 'threatens a collapse of the ceasefire in Gaza.' Mladenov said there is 'no better alternative to the current plan' and that a 'return to war would be devastating,' directing his warning at both parties as Gaza continued to see Israeli raids and strikes. He noted Morocco has agreed to contribute troops to the International Stabilisation Force (Turkey will not participate, with an initial contingent expected to arrive soon) and that the Board has secured $7 billion in reconstruction pledges, even as the National Committee for Gaza Administration has yet to formally assume governing responsibilities and Netanyahu continues to reject elements of the Board's 15-point roadmap.

title: Israel-Lebanon MOU Under Strain as Report Finds Hezbollah Disarmament Pilot Program Falling Short
detail: August 28, 2026 — Two months after Israel and Lebanon signed their US-brokered June memorandum of understanding, a report from the Meir Amit Intelligence and Terrorism Information Center found the pilot disarmament program in southern Lebanon 'has failed to deliver on the security commitments outlined in the MoU': the Lebanese Army has not demonstrated it can disarm Hezbollah or establish a state monopoly on weapons, Hezbollah-affiliated organizations (the Islamic Health Organization, Wa Ta'awanu) continue to operate openly inside the designated pilot zones, and legal restrictions bar the Lebanese Army from searching private properties used by Hezbollah. Israeli officials, per Walla, have privately warned Washington the pilot program failed and criticized Lebanese Armed Forces Chief of Staff Rudolf Heichal for avoiding confrontation with Hezbollah commanders. The friction compounds Defense Minister Israel Katz's earlier position — 'we will not withdraw from the security zone in Lebanon as long as Hezbollah is not disarmed' — which the US State Department has objected to as inconsistent with the framework's commitments against a permanent Israeli presence; the next round of Rome-hosted verification talks is set for early September.
